questions.q: What places did Moses tell Israel to destroy?
questions.a: They were to destroy all the places where the nations that Israel dispossessed had worshiped their gods.

questions.q: What does Yahweh instruct the people of Israel do to the name of the gods of the nations?
questions.a: He told Israel to destroy everything to do with those gods in order to remove their name from there.

questions.q: In what place were the people of Israel to bring their burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, and offerings?
questions.a: They were to go to the place that Yahweh their God would choose.

questions.q: What kinds of things were the people of Israel doing?
questions.a: They were doing whatever they thought was right.

questions.q: What kind of rest will Yahweh give to Israel when they go over the Jordan?
questions.a: He will give them rest by protecting them from all their surrounding enemies, so they will live in safety.

questions.q: What animals can Israel kill and eat?
questions.a: Israel can kill and eat domesticated animals where they are living.

questions.q: What was Israel not allowed to eat?
questions.a: Israel was not allowed to eat the blood, but must pour it out on the earth.

questions.q: Where was Israel told they could not eat their tithes and sacrifices?
questions.a: They were not allowed to eat what was intended for tithing or sacrificing where they lived.

questions.q: Where were the people of Israel to eat their tithes and sacrifices?
questions.a: They were to eat these offerings in the place that Yahweh their God will choose.

questions.q: What was Israel told be sure not to do?
questions.a: They were told to not forget to take care of the Levites.

questions.q: What can Israel eat when Yahweh their God enlarges their borders as he has promised them?
questions.a: Israel can eat the meat from the new land.

questions.q: What can Israel eat if the place that Yahweh their God chooses to put his name is too far from them?
questions.a: If the place that Yahweh Israel’s God chooses to put his name is too far from where they live, then they may kill some of their flock for sacrifices as well as to eat.

questions.q: Where did they consider the life of the animal?
questions.a: Israel was to consider the blood as the life of the animal and thus should not eat it with the meat.

questions.q: What is Israel instructed to take to the place that Yahweh chooses?
questions.a: Israel is to take the sacred things that they have and their offerings to the place that Yahweh chooses.

questions.q: What is to be done with the blood and the meat of the animals they offer as a burnt offering?
questions.a: They are to pour the blood out on the altar of Yahweh their God and eat the meat.

questions.q: What is Israel instructed to do so that it may go well with them and with their descendants after them?
questions.a: Israel is to listen to and obey all the words that Yahweh commands them and do what is good and right so that things may go well for them and their descendants forever.

questions.q: What does Yahweh instruct Israel to watch out for when God enables Israel to go in and dispossess the nations in the land and live there?
questions.a: Israel is to pay attention so that they are not trapped into serving the gods of those nations.

questions.q: What have the other nations done to their sons and daughters in order to worship the gods?
questions.a: The other nations have even burned their sons and daughters on altars to these other gods.

commentary.text: Monuments of idolatry to be destroyed.
The place of God's service to be kept.

Verses 1–4 Moses comes to the statutes he had to give in charge to Israel; and begins with such as relate to the worship of God. The Israelites are charged not to bring the rites and usages of idolaters into the worship of God; not under colour of making it better. We cannot serve God and mammon; nor worship the true God and idols; nor depend upon Christ Jesus and upon superstitious or self-righteous confidences.

The command to bring ALL the sacrifices to the door of the tabernacle, was now explained with reference to the promised land. As to moral service, then, as now, men might pray and worship every where, as they did in their synagogues. The place which God would choose, is said to be the place where he would put his name. It was to be his habitation, where, as King of Israel, he would be found by all who reverently sought him. Now, under the gospel, we have no temple or altar that sanctifies the gift but Christ only: and as to the places of worship, the prophets foretold that in every place the spiritual incense should be offered, Mal 1:11. Our Saviour declared, that those are accepted as true worshippers, who worship God in sincerity and truth, without regard either to this mountain or Jerusalem, Joh 4:21. And a devout Israelite might honour God, keep up communion with him, and obtain mercy from him, though he had no opportunity of bringing a sacrifice to his altar. Work for God should be done with holy joy and cheerfulness. Even children and servants must rejoice before God; the services of religion are to be a pleasure, and not a task or drudgery. It is the duty of people to be kind to their ministers, who teach them well, and set them good examples. As long as we live, we need their assistance, till we come to that world where ordinances will not be needed. Whether we eat or drink, or whatever we do, we are commanded to do all to the glory of God. And we must do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to the Father through him. They must not even inquire into the modes and forms of idolatrous worship. What good would it do them to know those depths of Satan? And our inward satisfaction will be more and more, as we abound in love and good works, which spring from faith and the in-dwelling Spirit of Christ.
